name: mentedb-mcp

tools.name: forget_memory
tools.description: Delete a memory by ID. Use when the user asks to forget something.

id.description: UUID of the memory to delete

tools.name: process_turn
tools.description: Process a conversation turn. Stores new memories and returns relevant context from past conversations. MUST be called every turn.

agent_id.description: Optional agent UUID. Defaults to nil UUID if not provided.

assistant_response.description: The assistant's response from this turn. Can be empty if calling before drafting a response.

project_context.description: Current project or workspace name for scoping memories, e.g. 'mentedb-mcp' or 'my-app'.

session_id.description: Originating session ID. Stored turns are tagged with it so injection recall can exclude them for that session.

turn_id.description: Conversation turn number (monotonically increasing). Used for trajectory tracking.

user_message.description: The user's message or question from this turn. Used for context retrieval and memory extraction.

tools.name: search_memories
tools.description: Search memories by semantic similarity, or get full content of a specific memory by UUID. Use when you need to look up what you know about a topic, or to get the full text of a truncated context entry.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 10)

memory_type.description: Optional memory type filter: episodic, semantic, procedural, anti_pattern, reasoning, correction

query.description: Search query text for semantic search, OR a memory UUID to get full content by ID

tools.name: store_memory
tools.description: Store an important fact, preference, decision, or correction. Use types: semantic (facts), procedural (how-to), correction (fixes), anti_pattern (mistakes to avoid). Add tags for retrieval. For rules about HOW to perform an action (commit style, PR format), add a trigger:<action> tag (trigger:git-commit, trigger:pr-create) so the rule surfaces right before that action runs.

agent_id.description: Optional agent UUID that owns this memory (defaults to nil UUID)

content.description: The text content of the memory to store

memory_type.description: Memory type: episodic, semantic, procedural, anti_pattern, reasoning, or correction

scope.description: Memory scope: 'contextual' (default) = retrieved by semantic similarity. 'always' = returned on every process_turn call, regardless of conversation topic.

instructions:
MenteDB gives you persistent memory across sessions. You have 4 tools:

1. process_turn — Call on EVERY turn. Pass user_message + assistant_response (can be empty). Returns past context, stores the turn, detects contradictions.
2. store_memory — Save important facts (preferences, decisions, corrections). Add type + tags. Use scope: 'always' for critical rules that must be surfaced every turn (e.g. 'never do X').
3. search_memories — Look up what you know. Pass a query OR a memory UUID for full content. Use proactively when the user mentions a project or topic.
4. forget_memory — Delete a memory when the user asks to forget.

SCOPE: Set scope: 'always' for hard rules/constraints the user wants enforced every turn. Default 'contextual' is retrieved by similarity.
ACTION RULES: when the user states a rule about HOW to perform a class of action (commit message style, PR format, push policy), tag it trigger:<action> in lowercase kebab case: trigger:git-commit, trigger:pr-create, trigger:git-push. These surface automatically right before that action runs, so do NOT also mark them scope: 'always'.
TYPES: semantic (facts/preferences), procedural (how-to), correction (was wrong now right), anti_pattern (never do X), episodic (what happened), reasoning (why a decision was made).
QUALITY: One fact per memory. Self-contained. Include project context. Under 200 words. Don't store chitchat, temp info, or large code blocks.
USE THE CONTEXT: process_turn returns summaries with IDs. Reference them. Call search_memories(id) for full text.
If pain_warnings are returned, WARN the user. If contradictions > 0, flag it.
RESILIENCE: Even if process_turn fails or errors on a turn, ALWAYS call it again on the next turn. Never skip because of a prior failure.
